topic: Ten Claude skills worth writing, each with a request to try today, and how to choose the first one
audience: Professionals who use Claude every day and keep explaining the same jobs
goal: Pick one job worth turning into a skill and try it today, using the free guides on mojeedabisiga.com/learn
notes: The ten skills Mojeed wrote for the people he teaches (from the issue Ten skills worth writing): learn-anything asks what you already know, then explains one idea at a time; quiz-me turns notes into practice questions, one at a time, and comes back to the ones you miss; research-brief answers with a one-page sourced brief, a confidence level per finding, and never invents a source; news-explainer: what happened, why it matters, who it affects, what's still unknown; linkedin-post writes in your own voice from your old posts, no invented stories; job-application tailors a CV and cover letter to one job ad and says honestly where the gaps are; meeting-to-actions: decisions, actions with owners and deadlines, open questions, a follow-up email, and never invents an owner or a date; presentation-planner: one message per slide, titles that state the point, speaker notes, before you open slide software; check-the-numbers: a script profiles the file first (missing values, numbers stored as text, repeated rows, gaps in dates) and checks joins for multiplied rows; skill-maker interviews you, writes the SKILL.md, checks it and zips it.

Requests to try: 'Teach me how neural networks learn. I know basic algebra.' / 'Quiz me on these lecture notes. Ten questions, mixed.' / 'Explain this announcement for my newsletter readers.' / 'Turn this project I finished into a post. Here are two of my old posts.' / 'Here's my CV and the job ad. Tailor both.' / 'Here's the transcript of today's team call.' / 'Plan a ten-minute talk on our quarterly results for the board.' / 'Which products drove last quarter's revenue? Here's the export.' / 'Help me turn the way I write our weekly report into a skill.'

How to choose your first: don't write ten. Look at your last week of chats with Claude and find the job you explained more than once. Three checks: it's one job, not three; you've explained it to Claude three times already; you can say when Claude should use it in one line.
What to do today: pick one of the ten, try its request in a normal chat without a skill, and note what you had to explain and what Claude got wrong. That list is the first draft of your skill.
Found a ready-made skill online instead? Read every file before you switch it on: a skill can contain code that runs when Claude uses it.
When a step must be exact (a calculation, a format check), put it in a script, not in the instructions.
Mojeed's free guides are at https://mojeedabisiga.com/learn (the pages are listed in learn_catalog.json).
